items.title: The Analyst Desk v3 — full coverage, locked lines, the pattern engine
items.tagline: Every analyst now reads every game, the pregame line is locked and shown on every card, a new pattern engine measures what the desk's agreement is actually worth (including the contrarian read), and the chief speaks in those measured numbers.
items.latest: 2026-07-30: shipped in one pass, four items, 479 serving checks green. (1) FULL COVERAGE — the board had 36 analyst no-reads this morning (VEGA silent on all 21 games because the champion engine froze no value play, SCOUT silent on 15). SCOUT now prices EVERY wall (T-24h→T-1h) the way ATLAS already did, and a new forced-coverage layer fills whatever is left: VEGA reads its own market microstructure (line move off the open → sharp-book divergence → de-vigged book-median lean, conviction capped at 0.53 and labelled low conviction in its own voice), ATLAS/SCOUT backfill from their own engines on the latest arrived pregame wall. Board today: 21/21 for all four analysts, ZERO no-reads. RECORDS DISCIPLINE: coverage reads carry a coverage_expanded flag with today's activation date and grade in their OWN ledger (record.coverage) — record.analysts is byte-identical to before. (2) THE PREGAME LINE, LOCKED — a new write-once store captures the market state at the last wall before first pitch (total, both totals prices, the run line and both run-line prices, book, wall, captured_at) and freezes it at first pitch; a locked record can never be rewritten. Every analyst read now carries vs_line — the exact number that engine was priced against — so a card can say 'ATLAS: OVER 8.5 (priced vs 8.5)' and flag when a voice is on a different number. A post-lock market move shows in line_now, separately, and never touches the locked block. Live games gain live_progress: score, inning, runs so far vs the locked total, pace, projected final, and p_hit_now — the probability the pregame pick still cashes — populated ONLY inside the live simulator's certified buckets (null and 'watching' outside them). Every live number is display-only and touches no record. (3) THE PATTERN ENGINE — the centrepiece Leon asked for: for every consensus configuration (4-0 unanimous; 3-1 keyed by WHICH analyst dissents; 2-2 keyed by WHICH PAIR sides together) × side, the graded n / W-L-P / hit rate / EXACT binomial (Clopper-Pearson) interval AND the contrarian read — what FADING that configuration would have done — plus all six pairwise-conditional patterns (agree and disagree). Two eras, computed separately and NEVER summed: the walk-forward reconstruction (325 all-four games, 2026-03-27→04-30) and the live era from today's activation (starts empty). The headline measurement: when all four agree the game has gone the OTHER way 59% of the time (n=34, reconstructed) — interval 0.25–0.59, so a coin flip, and the payload says so. Pattern maths verified against a hand-computed 12-game fixture and the exact interval cross-checked against scipy. (4) THE CHIEF USES IT — the DiamondEdge synthesis is now pattern-aware in its LANGUAGE and its confidence ordering: on a unanimous game where unanimity measures below 50% the chief says so and the displayed action drops one rung ('All four analysts lean over… and unanimous calls have gone the other way 59% of the time (n=34, reconstructed)'). Each card's chief block carries the pregame O/U call against the locked line, the run-line call, the predicted final score and the pattern-grounded rationale. Synthesis stays PRESENTATION/ROUTING ONLY — the pattern can only move an action DOWN the ladder, a PASS can never become a PLAY, and betting confidence remains solely the +EV gate + the star system. synthesis_config_version is now v2_live_patterns, regenerated nightly from the pattern engine with the static v1 artifact as the fallback.
items.detail: Modules: v4/serve/pregame_line.py (the locked pregame store + line_now), v4/serve/coverage.py (forced-coverage reads, own board + own ledger), v4/serve/consensus_patterns.py (the pattern engine + the nightly synthesis_config_v2 generator), plus multi-wall pricing in v4/serve/scout_stream.py and the pattern-aware chief in v4/serve/analyst_desk.py. Cycle wiring: the intraday serve captures/locks the pregame line and fills coverage; the overnight grades the coverage ledger and recomputes the pattern table + synthesis config AFTER every stream has graded, from GRADED LEDGERS ONLY. Rails held throughout: write-once picks, no existing record restated, the champion engine read-only, the sealed holdouts and the confirmation corpus never opened, no Odds API spend (every new number comes from the local point-in-time fact store or the free live poller), live numbers display-only. New suites: pregame_line 15 checks, coverage 18, consensus_patterns 28, analyst_desk +23, unified_model +37, daily_cycle +5 — 479 unified serving checks green.

items.title: The desk comes alive
items.tagline: The four analysts now talk: per-game takes in each persona's voice rendered from that engine's real numbers, a nightly desk recap with an analyst of the night, head-to-head rivalry scoreboards, and ATLAS re-pricing live games in-game — inside his certified range only.
items.latest: 2026-07-30: shipped in one iteration, everything grounded in real engine data. (1) ANALYST VOICES — every game card's four analysts now carry a 1-2 sentence take in their own voice (VEGA in market terms, ATLAS in simulation terms, NOVA in calibrated-probability terms, SCOUT in fundamentals terms), rendered from deterministic template libraries over that engine's ACTUAL served row; a validator extracts every number from every take and asserts it exists in the source row — nothing fabricated, ever, selftested on every rebuild. A lone dissenter argues back (dissent template class). (2) NIGHTLY DESK RECAP — once a slate grades, a write-once recap is stored: analyst of the night, per-analyst W-L lines, best and worst call quoted with the real final ('ATLAS said 60% over at 7.5 — it landed 14'), a consensus note and a verdict line; last 14 days ride the payload. (3) RIVALRY — head-to-head disagreement scoreboards for all six analyst pairs (only games both graded on opposite sides) plus Mon-Sun weekly standings with an analyst-of-the-week from completed weeks only. (4) LIVE ATLAS — during live games the certified conditional simulator re-prices P(over the pregame line) from the actual score/inning/base-out state, ONLY inside the fitness-certified buckets from the live-MC late round (the S guard blocks 2026 innings 7-9, so those states honestly say 'watching'); display only forever — never graded, never a bet, never touches any record. All rails selftested (345 unified checks green).
items.detail: The Analyst Desk's second act: presentation depth without a single new claim. Every voice line is a restatement of numbers that engine already published (the pick_reasons pattern extended into persona template libraries, ~10-12 templates each, seeded deterministic per game so regenerations are byte-stable). The recap, head-to-head and weekly standings are pure views over the SAME activation-dated graded ledgers the records already read — nothing re-graded, nothing restated, write-once where it matters. LIVE ATLAS runs the exact certified conditional engine (FIX-A..D + HFA, engine_late) with per-game tables built walk-forward from the sim stream's own as-of live corpus; certified-bucket membership mirrors the frozen m1b decision-point censor cell-for-cell and is selftested against the frozen certified corpus itself. Its market verdict in that territory was NULL, and the display says so: a transparent voice, not an edge. The underlying pick machinery, every record, the champion, and the sealed holdouts are untouched.

items.title: The Analyst Desk
items.tagline: Four named analysts — VEGA the Market Reader, ATLAS the Physicist, NOVA the Quant, SCOUT the Traditionalist — now call every game head-to-head, the desk states its consensus, and the DiamondEdge pick synthesizes their independent reads.
items.latest: 2026-07-30: the desk's full walk-forward audit is in (28,892 graded analyst-reads, leakage-audited, sealed stores untouched). Headlines: VEGA is the only analyst with a real measured record (51.8% on 8,534 reads, the only one that beats the market's own price; 54.8% in high-run parks across five straight seasons). When the three long-history analysts all agree they hit 52.5% on 2,065 games — real but too streaky to bet, so consensus stays presentation, never stake. And Leon's inversion question is answered: served picks ran 55.8% on 190 — no inversion, and no extra confidence either. Full plain-language write-up: v4/models/output/ANALYST_DESK_REPORT.md; measured synthesis rules v1 live in analyst_desk/synthesis_config_v1.json. Follow-on iteration 2026-07-30: 'The desk comes alive' (see desk_comes_alive) — persona takes, nightly recap, rivalry boards, live in-game ATLAS.
items.detail: Leon's product pivot: every model gets a name and an identity, and the home screen becomes a competition between them. All four analysts are REAL engines already serving — VEGA is the champion market engine (the live betting record), ATLAS the physical Monte Carlo simulator, NOVA the calibrated v4 model, SCOUT the honest-null simple-8 fundamentals model wired in as a new no-stars lean stream (walk-forward daily refit, its own write-once board and public ledger, activation 2026-07-30). The desk consensus covers both markets (totals for all four; run-line for the two margin voices, ATLAS + NOVA — VEGA and SCOUT honestly have no margin view). CONTINUITY RULE: the synthesis is presentation — the existing unified pick machinery keeps serving and grading underneath, its record continues unbroken, and where the desk says AVOID over a live pick, the pick still grades; it displays as the desk passing. A stricter coupling (the desk actually gating picks) waits for a measured, human-signed config (the synthesis_config_version hook), informed by the new consensus-history table — which starts sparse and says so. Also new: a pre-registered inversion check on the live served record (n>=150 trigger, exact binomial CI vs 0.50) that turns 'it feels like it's negatively predicting' into a falsifiable test. MEASURED (2026-07-30): the consensus-history table is no longer sparse — the desk's whole walk-forward history was assembled and audited. Core-3 desk (VEGA/ATLAS/SCOUT, 7,484 games 2022-2026): unanimous 52.5% [50.4, 54.8] but season-unstable (54-55% in 2024-25, ~coin-flip in 2022-23 and 2026); 2-1 majority 50.9% — a coin flip. All-4 window (thin, 391 games): unanimous 46.2% on 52, 3-1 46.3% on 218 — nothing playable or fadeable as a bet rule, which is exactly why synthesis rules v1 route presentation only: unanimous → prominent shared lean, 3-1 → majority with the dissenter named and no confidence language, 2-2 → the disagreement is the story. Personalities are now number-backed: VEGA the Market Reader is the desk's one certified specialist (51.8% overall, STRONG cells in high-run parks/high totals/late season); SCOUT the Traditionalist an honest 51.0% with no certified specialty; ATLAS the Physicist a 50.6% side-picker whose real value is independence (agrees with VEGA only 47% of the time) and run-distribution shape; NOVA the Quant 49.5% (2026-only), echoing SCOUT 68% of the time so it never double-counts. The pre-registered inversion check resolved early on the pooled record: 106/190 = 55.8%, day-clustered CI [44.8, 66.4] — the served picks are not negatively predictive, and the sample licenses no extra confidence in either direction. Staking remains 100% champion EV gate + stars; all conclusions provisional under the standing hygiene rule.

items.title: Spreads return (run lines)
items.tagline: Run-line calls are back on every game tile — as a brand-new stream that starts 0-0-0 and gets graded in public from day one.
items.latest: 2026-07-27: 11 run-line leans served today; the first graded results land tonight — record starts honest at 0-0-0
items.detail: Spreads were removed from the product on 07-07 and return on Leon's call as a NEW, separately-graded, activation-dated stream: the record starts 0-0-0 on 07-27, every stated side is locked at first pitch and graded at the real locked price, and nothing is retro-credited or blended with a backtest. Honesty posture: the stream is UNPROVEN and serves clearly-labeled LEANS only — never a bet. The run-line engine test that could have opened a bet path reported the same day: BLOCKED — the simulator (validated on totals) fails its margin fitness gate (it carries no home-field advantage), and even set aside, the de-vigged run-line market beat every declared arm on Brier, including the moneyline-only control. So the market's run-line price is genuinely informative and our leans are exactly that: leans, graded in public until something real is earned. The pre-pivot spread machinery was adjudicated a research null and is never revived as credit.

items.title: Simulator joins the board
items.tagline: A fully-physical Monte Carlo of every game — 20,000 simulated games per matchup — re-priced at every decision wall through the day (T-24h to T-1h) and shown on every game tile, tracked in public.
items.latest: 2026-07-30: the sim now re-prices at every decision wall (T-24h/T-12h/T-6h/T-3h/T-1h) as inputs firm up — each wall write-once, the latest wall locked at first pitch is what grades — so its read is visible all day, not just the T-3h hour. First graded day stands 9-6 on 15 leans — small-sample noise by its own measured tie-the-market baseline; record accrues in public
items.detail: Leon's call: 'add a monte carlo model.' The validated physical run simulator — every plate appearance drawn from empirical base-out transition tables tilted to the two lineups, starters, bullpens, park, weather and umpire as of the T-3h wall, with the home-field module ON and the walk-forward run-environment recalibration — prices P(over the posted total) for every game at each decision wall as it arrives (T-24h through T-1h; each wall written once, never revised; the latest wall locked at first pitch is what grades), from as-of inputs only — early walls ride the strictly-more-conservative D−2 enrichment per the wall-hygiene rule. THE HONEST PART, said loudly: in validation the simulator TIES the market (its blend-vs-market test came back a statistical tie, p=0.28, and its median lands within ~0.02 runs of the posted line). That is remarkable physics — an independent model of the game reproducing Vegas's number from first principles — but it is NOT an edge. So it serves as a transparent voice, never a bet: LEAN/PASS only, stars hard-capped at 1, is_bet always false, it never touches the headline pick, and its record starts 0-0-0 (activation 2026-07-28) in its own separately-graded lean ledger. An upgrade to a priced mode exists only behind a passing engine-vs-market report plus a human-signed state file — never automatic.

items.title: Better-calibrated confidence
items.tagline: The confidence number behind every score now means what it says — probabilities are re-checked against everything we've actually graded, every day.
items.latest: 07-27: live from today — served probabilities pass through a walk-forward calibration check fitted only on already-graded picks (7,001 of them). Past picks and records are untouched.
items.detail: Our research kept finding the same honest problem: the model's WIN/LOSS picking is real but its CONFIDENCE grading was not — measured out-of-sample, our probabilities ran overconfident and the star ladder didn't order results the way it claimed. This ships the fix the research validated: before a pick is scored, its probability is passed through a calibration map fitted ONLY on picks that were already graded before that day (never the day's own games, never the future). The map is deliberately humble — it can shrink or grow how boldly we disagree with Vegas, but it can never flip a pick's side and it refuses to learn 'unders are hot lately'. Practical effect: conviction is currently getting SHRUNK (the graded evidence says our disagreements were overstated), so expect fewer model picks, more honest PASSes, and scores that bunch lower. To be clear about what this is NOT: it does not create an edge and we claim none — it makes the confidence number honest, which is what the stars are built on. Old picks, scores and records are locked and never restated.
items.result: Live 07-27. Walk-forward Brier 0.24996 -> 0.24989, calibration Z 1.10 -> 0.54 on 6,424 replayed rows; model take-rate roughly halves. Not an edge — honesty.

items.title: Mega edge hunt
items.tagline: Runs a huge overnight sweep of 46 candidate betting ideas and fully builds the 12 strongest.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: all 12 fronts complete — zero survivors, nine doors closed for good
items.detail: The biggest sweep we have run: 97 ideas from 25 research angles, narrowed to the 12 strongest, each pre-registered and tested on old data only. Nothing earned money. The recurring lesson: where a retail book looks slow or generous, it is usually informed behavior or noise — and the real patterns we did find were already in the price. One old edge (shopping extreme prices vs the sharpest book) existed but died around 2023.
items.result: 0 of 12 fronts survived; 9 mechanisms permanently closed; banked facts feed future models

items.detail: Thirty-five ideas from the internet research sweep got a fast honest trial on old seasons we can afford to burn. None earned the right to touch the good data. Three patterns explain nearly every death: the books already price the effect (weather, umpires, parks, air density); the profit was really just one good season; or the idea only fires 20-80 times a year, too rare to ever prove.

items.title: Platoon splits data build

items.detail: Do batters facing a badly-matched starter (handedness splits) beat the total? The data build finished after weeks, and the test finally ran on 6,366 games. The tilt exists in the direction we predicted — but it is smaller than the vig, so it does not pay for itself at any book, and it is statistically indistinguishable from noise.

items.detail: The idea: first-inning (NRFI/YRFI) markets get less attention, so maybe they are softer. We built true first-inning pitcher form from pitch-level data and tested honestly on 4,609 out-of-sample games. The books price the first inning slightly BETTER than our data. All six pre-declared cells died. Together with the earlier probe, both natural angles are now closed — no future cycle needs to wonder about NRFI.

items.title: Sharp-book disagreement (whole family)
items.tagline: Four honest attempts to bet where our book disagrees with the sharpest book. Retired.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: the kill-test came back unproven, and the idea reverses on every book except the one we picked
items.detail: The premise was that our book hangs the stale number and the sharp book knows better. Tested directly on the exact games we would bet: our book was NOT measurably worse. Worse for the thesis, when you look across all bettable books the effect flips sign entirely — it only survives at the single book we had already picked for having the best returns, which is how false edges are born. The apparent signal traced back to one hot 49-bet stretch; remove two seasons and it inverts.
items.result: RETIRED after four honored stops — and the one-shot validation data was never spent

items.title: Does knowing the lineup help?
items.tagline: We cheated on purpose: handed the model the real batting order it could never know, and measured what it was worth.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: worth about nothing — and the market is just as accurate three hours before any lineup exists
items.detail: Rather than build better lineup predictions, we gave the model the actual nine hitters from the box score — information no bettor could ever have — across 8,300 games. A better lineup is worth about a quarter of a run raw, but the posted total already knows most of it, and the lineup we can project the day before captures ninety percent of the rest. What is genuinely new when the lineup posts moves the game by about a fiftieth of a run, and the book prices even that. Decisive check: the market forecasts just as well at six hours out, when zero lineups have posted, as at one hour out when nearly all have.
items.result: NULL — actual-vs-projected lineup worth +0.019 runs (CI includes zero); 0 of 33 tests beat the market; best honest ROI +0.02%

items.title: Can we just pick the right side?
items.tagline: Forget the fee — can we pick over/under better than a coin flip at all? Measured to the ceiling.
items.latest: 2026-07-26: best honest accuracy 51.5%, statistically indistinguishable from always betting under
items.detail: We changed the goal entirely: stop optimising for profit, just try to pick the winning side as often as possible. Best result across 8,412 games was 51.5%, with an error range that includes the strategy "always bet under" — a rule requiring no model at all. The most accurate rule we found was simply copying the market own side (52.1%), and even that falls short of the 52.4% needed to break even at standard pricing. Our confidence ranking is flat: keeping only the games we feel best about does not improve accuracy.
items.result: NULL — 51.5% ceiling (CI 50.5-52.6%) vs 50.6% for always-under; 0 of 26 pre-declared segments survived correction

items.title: The simulator vs derived markets
items.tagline: Pointed our validated game simulator at First-5 totals, run lines, and team-total ladders.
items.latest: 2026-07-27: home-field advantage added and validated; run line re-tested and closed NULL — the market beats the simulator even fixed
items.detail: First-5: the five-inning simulator passed every physics check, and its median lands within 0.06 runs of the posted line — same story as full games; closed. Run line: the simulator reproduces the strange texture of baseball margins almost perfectly but does not know home teams are better (it only knows they bat last) — a real, fixable defect. Team totals: we proved the book generates its ladders by formula, and that its own ladder, total, and moneyline disagree by 1.5-2 points on every game — a measured inconsistency, but with zero graded outcomes collected yet, no honest test is possible.
items.result: F5 NULL (3rd mechanism); run line NULL after the home-field fix (market sharper, 0 survivors); TT ladder inconsistency real but awaits data

items.title: Player form + momentum, combined
items.tagline: Fifty player-form signals — hot bats, pitcher stuff trends, bullpen state — combined into one model, aimed at totals and spreads.
items.latest: 2026-07-27: the combined model is WORSE than the market line, every season, on both markets
items.detail: The fair critique was that player momentum signals had only been tested one at a time. So all fifty were combined into one model and aimed at both the totals market and the newly-returned spread market across 9,230 games. Result: the combined model is significantly worse than the market price on both, every season, both favorite and dog sides. The spread market is at least as sharp as totals. By the time we can bet, player form is in the price.
items.result: DOUBLE NULL — totals composite ΔBrier +0.0018 worse (CI excludes zero); run-line market beats fundamentals AND player-state every season; spread market NOT softer

items.title: Live in-game repricing (Monte Carlo)
items.tagline: Re-price the total mid-game from the live state, against 19.2M historical in-play quotes.
items.eta: closed (early innings); late innings blocked on calibration
items.latest: 2026-07-27: in the corner where the engine is certified, the live market wins clean — and it is signal, not execution friction
items.detail: The one Monte Carlo surface never tested. Where the simulator is provably calibrated (early innings, normal scoring), the live market beat it even at zero execution cost — a flat coin-flip baseline nearly ties the market and beats our sim there. Crucially the test separated "no edge" from "edge eaten by slow execution": it is no edge, so faster pipes would not help. The honest asterisk: the territory where the founding mid-game folklore lives (late innings, hot high-scoring games) was never tested because the engine is provably miscalibrated there — that corner is blocked, not closed.
items.result: NULL in certified states (frictionless leg also null; -3.2% executable); late/hot states BLOCKED pending four named calibration fixes

items.title: Simulator home-field fix
items.tagline: Taught the simulator that home teams are actually better — validated, and it still does not beat the run-line market.
items.latest: 2026-07-27: home-win rate now matches reality (53.6% vs 53.1% empirical); one defect remains in extra-inning walk-off modeling
items.detail: The engine knew home teams bat last but not that they win more. Fixed from training data only, with no regression to everything already validated. The re-test still closed honest null: the run-line market beats even the fixed simulator, confirming that market is actively priced, not derived. The remaining walk-off quirk is documented; fixing it would improve the instrument but the evidence says it would not create an edge.
items.result: Location fixed and validated; run-line front closed NULL; margin engine not yet certified (1-run region), spread stream stays leans-only

items.title: The last corner: late-inning live totals
items.tagline: Recalibrated the engine for late, high-scoring, hot games — the founding folklore territory — and tested it clean.
items.latest: 2026-07-27: all four calibration fixes worked; the certified engine now TIES the live market at the flagged instant — and loses at any price you could actually get
items.detail: This was the one corner never tested, with zero peeks: late innings, high-scoring environments, hot games. The calibration round genuinely fixed the engine (the 0.9-run under-projection closed to near zero). The result: our simulator now knows exactly as much as the live late-inning market — and nothing more. At executable prices the book is decisively ahead in every bucket, season, side, and book. The map of our markets is complete.
items.result: NULL in all three certified buckets; frictionless LATE is a genuine tie (zero edge); executable -4.5% over 26,320 bets. The keepers: a certified conditional engine and a fitness harness.
